body: > * An alternative would be to completely sync 3.x with the current 4.x version of Godot WASAPI code, but that seems to offer more bug potential. > > * I must admit this has made me rethink about whether these changes are safe to cherry pick to 3.6 stable, or whether they need more time to stew in master first. It's been on my TODO list since we last talked about this to port over #100116, which fixes a number of memory leaks. Unfortunately, calendar 2026 is especially busy for me and I've been overwhelmed with too many responsibilities to do this. I'm hopeful that I can port over that PR in 2027 at some point. But obviously, that's not a great timeline. > To me the whole `thread_func()` here looks messy with all the nested if statements (hence the reason for this bug being introduced) and might benefit from being broken up into functions. At a glance, this looks like it has its foundation as a copy-paste of an official Windows sample project, except reworked to use nesting ifs instead of `goto` statements. Take that as you will. > * I'd let to get this double-checked and tested by someone from 4.x audio (@allenwp ? ) both because I can't test it (being Linux here) and because 3.x has diverged significantly from 4.x in this file. Because the existing 3.x branch has the same `if (invalidated) {` flow, I can't see how this change would introduce any issues that wouldn't also be introduced by the the same change that has been merged into 4.x. This flow happens when you simply unplug an audio device. Anyway, I tested this PR using the Checks artifact. |3.x branch head's [Checks build](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/31681637661) | This PR | --|-- | Audio continued to play fine throughout in both of these cases, only noticeable difference in behaviour was not getting the error message anymore: This is the expected behaviour from this fix.
